change: Added Gluteus Medius to primary glutes entry. The figure-four position crosses one ankle over the opposite knee, placing the hip in external rotation and abduction, which strongly recruits the Gluteus Medius of the planted leg in addition to Gluteus Maximus. This is a de-facto unilateral/asymmetric movement so the obliques secondary is appropriate and retained.

Removed oblique secondary. This is a bilateral, symmetric movement; there is no meaningful anti-rotation demand that would justify External/Internal Obliques as secondary muscles. Hamstrings, Erector Spinae, and abs (isometric bracing) secondaries are retained.

Added Gluteus Medius as a separate secondary entry. EMG and biomechanics research confirms the gluteus medius is a critical pelvic stabilizer during single-leg work, preventing the free-side hip from dropping. It is distinct from the primary Gluteus Maximus and warrants its own secondary slot.

Added Gluteus Medius as a separate secondary entry. The staggered (B-stance) variant is quasi-unilateral (~70% load on the working leg), so the Gluteus Medius must stabilize the pelvis. Obliques secondary retained as the asymmetric loading creates an anti-rotation demand.

No change. Floor press at horizontal angle correctly targets both Sternal Head (dominant) and Clavicular Head as co-primary. Triceps Brachii co-primary is confirmed — floor press is well-documented as more triceps-dominant than bench press. Anterior Deltoids secondary is correct. Data verified.
